spatial_claims.claim: Diagonals AC and BD of square ABCD meet inside the square at point O
Diagonal AC bisects the right angles at vertices A and C (angle BAC = angle DAC, angle BCA = angle DCA) via SAS congruence of triangles ABC and ADC
Diagonal BD bisects the right angle at vertex B (angle ABD = angle CBD) via SAS congruence of triangles BAD and BCD
OE is perpendicular to AB with foot E strictly on segment AB (not at endpoints or beyond)
OF is perpendicular to BC with foot F strictly on segment BC
OG is perpendicular to CD with foot G strictly on segment CD
OH is perpendicular to DA with foot H strictly on segment DA
OE = OH via AAS congruence of triangles AEO and AHO (equal bisected angles at A, right angles at feet, common side AO)
OE = OF via AAS congruence of triangles BEO and BFO (equal bisected angles at B, right angles at feet, common side BO)
OF = OG via AAS congruence of triangles CFO and CGO (equal bisected angles at C, right angles at feet, common side CO)
Circle with center O and radius OE passes through E, F, G, H (all on the circle)
Each side of the square is perpendicular to the radius at its contact point, so by 3.16 each side touches the circle without cutting it (tangency)

configuration_map: O is the intersection of diagonals AC and BD, located at the center of square ABCD, inside the square. The diagonals bisect the right angles at each vertex (each bisected angle is 45 degrees). E, F, G, H are the feet of perpendiculars from O to sides AB, BC, CD, DA respectively, each lying strictly on its side-segment (at the midpoint by symmetry). The four perpendicular distances OE, OF, OG, OH are all equal, establishing a circle centered at O passing through all four feet. Each side is perpendicular to the radius at the contact point, making it tangent to the circle. The configuration is that of a square with its incircle, centered at the intersection of the diagonals.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. O at the center of the square is correctly established via diagonal intersection. The angle bisection properties follow validly from SAS congruences. The perpendicular feet are correctly shown to lie on the side-segments. The equal distances follow from valid AAS congruences. The tangency argument via 3.16 is correctly applied. No angle decomposition as a sum appears in the proof, so the primary error pattern does not arise. No point is used in contradictory positions.
